title: Threshold-Based Evaluation
learning_outcomes: Explain threshold-based evaluation and accurately refer to at least two syllabus subtopics.
Apply the main idea of threshold-based evaluation to a small example, trace, calculation, or scenario.
Identify one important assumption or failure mode and describe how to check it.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study threshold-based evaluation in the context of model evaluation and optimization. You will connect the PDF subtopics to a small example and practice describing what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Threshold-Based Evaluation matters because it affects how data is collected, represented, analyzed, interpreted, or used in a decision. Check the task and assumptions before choosing a method.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Evaluation translates model behavior into evidence against a defined baseline. Match metrics to the task and inspect subgroup failures, calibration, costs, and variation.

items.title: Decision thresholds
items.text: Define decision thresholds in relation to threshold-based evaluation; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

items.title: Precision–recall trade-offs
items.text: Work through precision–recall trade-offs using a small, synthetic example before scaling up. State what the calculation or method returns and why that result is useful.

items.title: Sensitivity and specificity
items.text: Check the edge cases for sensitivity and specificity: missing values, unusual ranges, different groups, time boundaries, or a changed input can affect the conclusion.

items.title: ROC curves
items.text: Document the rule or choice for roc curves so another learner can reproduce the analysis and understand its limitations.

items.text: Define precision–recall curves in relation to threshold-based evaluation; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Restate the question addressed by threshold-based evaluation. 2. Identify the input data, intended output, and assumptions. 3. Predict what the small example should show before reading its output. 4. Change one input or assumption, compare the result, and document what remains uncertain.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the provided synthetic input, rerun or retrace the example, and change one value at a time. Do not use personal records, credentials, or data you are not authorized to access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Keep the question, data grain, units, and assumptions explicit. If a result differs, inspect the input and steps in order. Avoid turning an observed association into a causal claim, treating a sample as the population, or assuming a small demonstration guarantees production behavior. A monitoring metric should have a denominator, a time window, and a defined response.

content_blocks.title: Responsible interpretation
content_blocks.text: This example is a teaching aid. It is static in the CodeLeaf lesson and is not executed in the browser. It uses small synthetic values; validate any real workflow in a separate, appropriate local environment and protect sensitive data.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small synthetic example for threshold-based evaluation. State a question, make a prediction, trace or run an appropriate calculation, then write one finding and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: Refer accurately to the topic and its syllabus subtopics.
Record a reproducible example or a complete manual trace with an expected result.
Document at least one assumption, limitation, data-quality issue, or evaluation check.
hints: Write down the input, expected result, units, and assumptions first.
Change only one condition when testing a revised example.
Ask whether the data and method represent the real decision; do not infer causality or production readiness from a toy example.
troubleshooting: Check input values, path assumptions, package versions, indentation, and units.
For SQL, use a local schema and read-only test data; this page does not provide a live database.
For package-dependent work, create an isolated environment and use the relevant official documentation.
